recent_posts.title: Behind Japan’s Warnings of a Cyber Crisis
recent_posts.text: Explore Japan's 2026 cyber crisis, rising breach trends, AI tooling, legacy systems, and key mitigation strategies to protect organizations. Reporting on cyberattacks against Japanese entities rose 48% between Q2 and Q3 2026, encompassing ransomware, exploitation of vulnerabilities, credential leaks, and service disruptions. Significant incidents exposed millions of customer records and disrupted operations across multiple sectors, with attacks on shared service providers extending the impact to downstream organizations. Further incidents in October 2026 indicate that these trends have persisted into Q4. This report examines potential contributing factors, including demand for Japanese personal information, legacy systems, software vulnerabilities, weak API controls, and AI’s likely role in lowering technical and language barriers. New incident-reporting requirements under Japan’s Active Cyber Defense (ACD) law, effective October 1, may further increase the number of disclosures of incidents affecting Japanese organizations.

recent_posts.title: Signal bug could let someone keep listening after you hang up
recent_posts.text: A flaw in Signal’s calling library could let another participant keep hearing you after you hang up. Update your app to get the latest fixes. A recently disclosed flaw in Signal’s calling software could allow another participant to keep hearing you after you hang up. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-113380 ( CVSS score 9.3 out of 10), affects RingRTC versions earlier than 2.72.0. RingRTC is the open-source library behind Signal’s voice and video calling functionality, providing calling components for its mobile and desktop applications. The flaw concerns how Signal’s calling library shuts down a call. It does not affect how it encrypts conversations. According to the published vulnerability description , another participant could overwhelm a call’s internal event queue and interfere with the steps that should disconnect it when you end the call. The main concern is unwanted listening after someone believes a conversation has ended. If a malicious call participant successfully triggered the flaw, they could potentially continue hearing audio that the other person no longer intended to share. recent_posts.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation: Two Critical PHP Flaws Explained
recent_posts.text: Two critical PHP remote code execution flaws (PHP2Shell) are reportedly being exploited. See who’s exposed, how the exploits work, and how to remediate now. Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in the PHP engine, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (nicknamed “PHP2Shell”), are reportedly being targeted in active exploitation attempts following the leak of technical details ahead of PHP’s October 21, 2026, security release. Because the flaws affect PHP itself rather than a specific application, websites running vulnerable PHP versions may be exposed, including those built on WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla. This post covers PHP’s advisories, exploitation reports, public proof-of-concept exploits, exposure data, and patching guidance, along with details from the TTP Instance Insikt Group® published to customers. Attack Surface Intelligence signatures for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are available to Recorded Future customers. Organizations running PHP should patch immediately.

recent_posts.title: Scammers are finding new ways to target your phone. Here are 5 ways to protect yourself
recent_posts.text: One in three people now tune out scam warnings, and scammers are counting on it. The warnings are everywhere these days. Don’t click this. Don’t open that. Don’t scan this. Don’t download that. These messages of caution, however well-intended, are so ubiquitous and constant that it should come as no surprise that some people have started to tune them out. How many people? About one in three, according to our recent study . Keeping up with every warning can feel exhausting. Meanwhile, scammers are finding new ways to target people and phones give them plenty of opportunities. Mobile phones give scammers multiple ways to reach people, from text messages and calls to social media posts. According to a 2022 Federal Communications Commission report cited by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), texting is a more common communication method than voice or email. Criminals appear to be taking advantage of that fact. Consumers reported losing $470 million to text scams in 2024, up 26% from $373 million the year before and more than five times the amount reported in 2020. recent_posts.text: The defect in a widely distributed open-source library provoked an emergency response, yet exploitation hasn’t been observed in the wild. The post Experts temper emergency-level alarms over critical Brotli defect appeared first on CyberScoop . Alarm bells ratcheted up yet again about an AI-discovered vulnerability that could — if exploited in the wild — destabilize vast stretches of the internet. The critical defect — CVE-2026-111497 — affects the Google-developed Brotli decompression library that’s bundled into many components, applications and cloud services riding on open-source software. The buffer overflow vulnerability, which OpenAI Codex Security discovered and Node.js disclosed in a Oct. 21 security advisory , can trigger system crashes and remote code execution. Researchers haven’t observed any active exploitation of the defect in real networks, but concerns are mounting. recent_posts.title: Artificial Intimacy: Love and lies in the age of AI
recent_posts.text: Our latest report reveals how AI is reshaping our relationships, blurring what feels authentic, and creating new ways for intimacy to be exploited. AI is becoming a third wheel in relationships, increasingly playing a role in the most intimate parts of our lives. It shows up in the flirty first text, the polished dating profile, the therapized language we use with a partner after a fight, the strength we gather after heartbreak, and everywhere in between. For some, AI is a source of companionship itself. And even if you’re not personally an AI user, you may still be dating, loving, arguing with, or trusting someone who is. As AI moves deeper into our relationships, it’s reshaping connection, blurring what feels authentic, and creating new ways for intimacy to be exploited. AI is starting to replace human interaction AI is moving into emotional territory once reserved for other people. For some, it’s no longer just a tool, but a source of support, companionship, and even romantic connection. recent_posts.title: Japan Adopts Proactive Cyber Defense Strategy
recent_posts.text: Learn about Japan's Active Cyber Defense (ACD) strategy, mandatory reporting rules, and key impacts on critical infrastructure. Executive Summary Japan’s Active Cyber Defense (ACD) framework shifts the country from voluntary information sharing and post-incident investigation to mandatory reporting, preventive communications analysis, and limited disruption of attack infrastructure. Beginning October 1, 2026, designated critical infrastructure operators must notify the government about covered systems and report qualifying incidents; those with existing systems have six months to submit initial notifications. New authorities that allow the government to collect and act on communications information (通信情報) will not take effect until November 23, 2027. The transition comes amid persistent Chinese strategic collection, North Korean revenue-driven cyber operations, and Russian cyber espionage. In cases directly linked to Japan, indicators related to these threat activities were frequently observed among victims, overseas affiliates, vendors, carriers, hosting providers, and government agencies. recent_posts.text: How AI helps collect data, deanonymize users, and link their accounts — and what to do to protect yourself from doxing and harassment. Anonymous imageboards have long been places where users could chat under pseudonyms without revealing their real names. But now people on these forums are discussing and testing AI tools for doxing — that is, for finding, matching, and publishing users’ data without their consent. Often this goes hand in hand with stalking the victim, hacking their accounts, bullying, and blackmail, and ultimately leads to a damaged reputation or even worse . In this post, we explain how artificial intelligence helps malicious actors leak other people’s data — and how to stand up for your right to online privacy. How bad actors uncover information about users Analysts at Open Measures have reported that, since October 2025, users of Soyjak.party , an imageboard popular with young people on the far right, have been discussing and using AI to deanonymize other users. Their victims are often activists, bloggers, and members of other “hostile” forums. recent_posts.text: Artem Stryzhak participated in a series of ransomware attacks on hospitals, government entities and law firms from the middle of 2018 to late 2021. The post Prolific Hive and Nefilim ransomware affiliate sentenced to 70 months in prison appeared first on CyberScoop . A 36-year-old Ukrainian national was sentenced to 70 months in prison for participating in a string of ransomware attacks targeting various critical infrastructure operators and businesses from the middle of 2018 to late 2021, the Justice Department said Tuesday. Artem Aleksandrovych Stryzhak was involved in ransomware attacks on hospitals that disrupted patient care, government entities, a dentist office, a company in the oil and gas transportation industry and law firms.
